subject: Art & Design
title: What Is Typography and Why It Matters
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is Typography and Why It Matters.

hook.text: You've never noticed good typography. But you've definitely noticed bad typography.

buildup.text: Typography is the art of arranging text so it's readable, functional, and emotionally right.

discovery.text: It's not just font choice. It's size, spacing, alignment, hierarchy — every decision about how text looks.

twist.text: Studies show readers judge a website's credibility in 50 milliseconds. Typography drives that snap judgment.

climax.text: Good typography is invisible. Bad typography screams. The goal is to never be noticed.

punchline.text: If you notice the type, it's already failed.

quiz.question: What is the goal of good typography?
options: To be invisible — serving content without being noticed
To use the most creative fonts possible
To make text as large as possible

details.summary: Typography is the art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and visually appealing. It influences how messages are perceived — the same words in different typefaces convey different emotions, authority levels, and brand personalities.
details.whyItMatters: Typography carries the unspoken tone of voice in every text. A hospital using Comic Sans or a law firm using a playful script would undermine their credibility instantly. Typography is the first impression every written communication makes.
takeaways: Typography makes written language legible, readable, and appealing
Different typefaces convey different emotions and authority
It's the unspoken tone of voice for all written communication

faq.question: Is typography the same as choosing a font?
faq.answer: Font selection is just one part of typography. Typography encompasses sizing, spacing, line length, hierarchy, alignment, color, pairing, and the overall arrangement of text. Choosing a font is like choosing an instrument; typography is composing the entire piece of music.

faq.question: Why should non-designers care about typography?
faq.answer: Everyone creates documents — emails, presentations, reports, social posts. Bad typography makes content harder to read and less credible. Good typography is invisible; it lets the message come through clearly. Understanding basic principles improves every piece of text you produce.
